title: Managing a Stage Boundary in Context

header.html: 4.6.1 apply managing a stage boundary: activities, inputs and outputs, roles and responsibilities, how the practices are applied; 4.6.2 analyze whether the activities, roles and responsibilities are effective and fit for purpose, considering tailoring, the practices, and the purpose and objectives of the process
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

toc.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves

html:
1Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves

Managing a stage boundary is the process the project manager uses near the end of a stage so the board can decide about the next one. The figure shows the flow.

Purpose: give the board enough information to review the success of the current stage, approve the next stage plan, review the updated project plan and confirm continued business justification and acceptable risk.

Objectives: the board is assured that the stage's products are complete and approved; the next stage plan, project plan and business case are updated; lessons are recorded; authorization for the next stage is requested.

The process is also used when the board asks for an exception plan. It is not used at the end of the last stage, which closing a project handles.

Principle How it shows up here
Manage by stages Each stage ends with a board decision before the next begins
Continued business justification The business case is refreshed and re-checked
Manage by exception An exception plan replaces a plan that would be exceeded
Focus on products The report shows which products were completed and approved
Exam tip

. Stage boundary means: review this stage, plan the next, confirm the business case, and the board decides. The project manager never authorizes the next stage.

2Activities, inputs and outputs

The names below give the general idea; check the Official Book's wording for the activities.

Activity What the project manager does
Plan the next stage Prepares the next stage plan in detail, with products, resources, tolerances and risks
Update the project plan Adds actuals and approved changes, and re-forecasts the remaining stages
Update the business case Refreshes costs, benefits and risks, and checks the project is still justified
Report stage end Writes the end stage report: performance against the plan, products approved, issues, risks, lessons
Produce an exception plan When the board asks after an exception, replaces the plan that would be exceeded
Flow Main items
Inputs The current stage plan and actuals; the project plan; the business case; product approvals; the project log; the board's request for an exception plan
Outputs End stage report; next stage plan or exception plan; updated project plan and business case; updated risk register; lessons; a request to authorize the next stage
Exam tip

. An exception plan replaces the plan that will be exceeded, and the board asks for it. A stage plan covers the next stage only.

3Roles

Role Area of focus in this process
Project manager Responsible: prepares the report, plans and updates; asks the board to decide
Team managers Give estimates and detail for the next stage's work
Executive Owns the business case and checks it still justifies the project
Senior user Confirms user needs and expected benefits still hold
Senior supplier Confirms the supplier can deliver the next stage plan
Project board Reviews the information and decides, in directing a project
Project assurance Reviews the report, plans and business case independently
Project support Collects actuals, updates registers, assembles documents

Check the book's roles table. If a plan would breach the project tolerances, the board goes to the corporate or programme level.

4How the practices are applied

Practice How it is applied at a stage boundary
Business case Update costs and benefits; check benefits are still expected and justified
Organization Check the team and roles still suit the next stage
Plans Next stage plan in detail; project plan updated; exception plan if asked
Quality Confirm products are approved; set quality needs for the next stage
Risk Re-assess risks and exposure; update the risk register
Issues Review open issues; carry forward or close them
Progress End stage report; tolerances for the next stage; lessons

5Judging a scenario

Effective approach Red flag: not fit for purpose
The report compares actuals with the plan and gives the board enough to decide A bulky or thin report, or one sent for information only
Business case, benefits and risks re-checked with current figures Business case left as it was at initiation
Next stage planned in detail, later stages in outline All remaining stages planned in detail, or no next stage plan
Project plan updated for the effect on later stages Project plan unchanged, or tolerance quietly extended
Exception plan produced when the board asks A new stage plan used to hide an overspend
The board decides before the next stage starts The next stage starts before authorization
Lessons used in the next stage plan Lessons ignored

Tailoring changes the form, not the decision:

  • Stage lengths: shorter stages give more control where risk or uncertainty is high; longer ones suit stable work. A project needs at least two management stages.
  • Management and technical stages: a management stage is a board control point. A technical stage groups work by skill or product type, such as design or build, and can overlap others. A technical stage ending is not a board decision point.
  • Small projects: a short report and one meeting, with decisions recorded.
  • Agile or incremental delivery: align a boundary with a release and replan from what was delivered.
  • Sustainability, digital and data: re-check sustainability measures and data risks.
Exam tip

. Board decisions belong to management stages, not technical stages. Do not add a formal board gate each time a technical stage finishes.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1The build stage of Project Harbor ends in two weeks. To save time, Sam Okafor asks Delta Software to start the pilot stage before the board has reviewed the end stage report. Was this an appropriate action for the project manager to take, and why?

  • AYes, because the next stage plan was already prepared and agreed
  • BYes, because the current stage is due to end within two weeks
  • CNo, because project assurance must sign the end stage report first
  • DNo, because only the board can authorize the next stage to start
Show the answer

Answer: D. The board authorizes each stage in directing a project, so work on the next stage waits for its decision (manage by stages).

S2At the end of the pilot stage, Project Harbor's business case still shows the costs and permit fees from initiation. Delta Software has since raised its price, and fewer berths will use the service. What should Sam do?

  • ALeave the business case unchanged until the project closes
  • BUpdate the business case and send it with the end stage report
  • CAsk the senior supplier to cut the price so nothing changes
  • DAsk project assurance to approve the business case for the board
Show the answer

Answer: B. The stage boundary refreshes the business case so the board can confirm continued justification.

S3After an exception report, the board asks Sam Okafor for an exception plan. Sam writes one that replaces the rest of the current stage plan, starts from the actuals to date, and shows the revised cost, end date and effect on the business case. Was this an appropriate action, and why?

  • AYes, because an exception plan replaces the plan being exceeded
  • BYes, because an exception plan only needs the next stage in outline
  • CNo, because the current stage plan must stay in place beside it
  • DNo, because an exception plan should leave the business case unchanged
Show the answer

Answer: A. An exception plan replaces the plan that would be exceeded, starts from the actuals and shows the board the effect.

S4Sam Okafor has sent the board the end stage report and the next stage plan for the pilot stage. Project tolerances are not forecast to be exceeded. Who decides whether the pilot stage can start?

  • ASam Okafor, the project manager
  • BJon Park, from project support
  • CThe project board as a group
  • DBrightwater's corporate level
Show the answer

Answer: C. The project board authorizes each stage, and corporate management is involved only if project tolerances would be exceeded.

S5Before deciding on the pilot stage, the board of Project Harbor wants to see how the build stage performed against its plan, which products were approved and what was learned. Which management product gives this?

  • AHighlight report
  • BException report
  • CEnd project report
  • DEnd stage report
Show the answer

Answer: D. The end stage report reviews the stage that is ending; the end project report covers the whole project only at closure.

S6Delta Software's design work, a technical stage, finishes in week 8 of the 12-week build stage. Sam asks the board for a formal stage boundary decision at that point. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because every technical stage must end with a board decision
  • BNo, because the board decides at management stages, not technical ones
  • CYes, because the board must approve each product as soon as it is complete
  • DNo, because stage boundaries are only used at the end of the project
Show the answer

Answer: B. The board's control points are management stages, and a technical stage grouping work by skill is not one.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the purpose of managing a stage boundary?

Show the answer

To give the board enough information to review the stage, approve the next stage plan and confirm continued business justification.

R2When is managing a stage boundary not used?

Show the answer

At the end of the last stage, which uses closing a project.

R3Name the five activities.

Show the answer

Plan the next stage, update the project plan, update the business case, report stage end and produce an exception plan.

R4What is an exception plan?

Show the answer

A plan that replaces the one that would be exceeded, produced when the board asks for it.

R5Name two outputs of the process.

Show the answer

The end stage report and the next stage plan.

R6What is a technical stage?

Show the answer

A grouping of work by skill or product type, not a board decision point.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose board reviews the stage, approves the next stage plan, confirms the business case
When near the end of every stage except the last
Activities plan the next stage, update plan and business case, report stage end, exception plan
Outputs end stage report, next stage plan, updated plan and business case, lessons
Effective enough information, benefits and risks re-checked, decision first
Red flags stale business case, next stage starts early, exception hidden in a stage plan
Tailoring stage length, management versus technical stage, lighter reports
